notes: IRQB is driven low while IRQ_STATUS & IRQ_MASK is nonzero; IRQ_TRIGGERED (bit 15) mirrors that state.
Reading IRQ_STATUS_L ($FFF0) clears every IRQ_STATUS bit and releases IRQB. IRQ_STATUS_H ($FFF1) has no side effect, so read it first when the high bits matter.

bits.name: IRQ_ERROR
bits.description: An error was pushed into the error queue.

bits.name: IRQ_IDXA_WRAPPED
bits.description: The active index in window A wrapped and its WRAP_IRQ flag was enabled.

bits.name: IRQ_IDXB_WRAPPED
bits.description: The active index in window B wrapped and its WRAP_IRQ flag was enabled.

bits.name: IRQ_COMMAND
bits.description: Command handler completed; asynchronous commands may raise it again on actual completion.

bits.name: IRQ_SPEED_CHANGED
bits.description: A requested PHI2 speed change was applied.

bits.name: IRQ_INPUT_KEYBOARD
bits.description: Enabled keyboard, consumer, or text input event pending.

bits.name: IRQ_AUDIO_SEQ_DONE
bits.description: A sequenced voice's track finished: it reached END, an unrecognized opcode, or its decode/catch-up budget.

bits.name: IRQ_TRIGGERED
bits.description: Aggregate state maintained by MIA when any masked IRQ flag is pending.
